title: Clo User Story - Institut Teknologi Bandung 🏫
description:
We take you inside Bandung Institute of Technology to see how the next generation of Indonesian designers are revolutionizing the fashion industry using CLO software.

For this year’s Kriya ITB Fashion Week (KIFW), textile and fashion design students shifted from traditional pattern-making to a fully digital workflow. Using CLO’s powerful 3D garment simulation, students prototyped, draped, and perfected their designs in a virtual space before cutting a single piece of fabric for their physical collection. The result? Unprecedented creative freedom, drastically reduced fabric waste, and a stunning physical runway showcase.

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server:https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us

---

transcript: Welcome to day one of CREA ITB Fashion Week 2026. CLAW is here to empower students to develop their knowledge in fashion, textile, and CREA. With CLAW 3D itself, you can express different types of soft goods, such as clothes, details, necklaces, bags. Everything that has patterns and is sewn can be visualized on our software. As a fourth generation university, we have to develop universities by research. One of them is with CLAW. We can research that in the future we need technology that is much higher, one of which is through digital. How do students or fashion engineers can pursue efficiency in working in the world of fashion or textile? By using CLAW 3D, they have the opportunity to show their work in the media or in a wider network. CLAW 3D is very helpful in creating patterns, then to simulate how the fabric is sewn, and also how the fabric sticks to the fabric. Like that. It's faster, it doesn't take too much time, and it can be simulated right away. And we can see the pattern right away, how the result turns out, and it's very easy. And maybe I will use CLAW 3D for that. Maybe at first we didn't know how to abstract ideas. Then it's visualized through 2D patterns and 3D patterns, so it looks like this is the final result. If there are still changes, for example, we can change it without... We have to sew it again, or we don't have the materials. So the process is simpler. So CLAW 3D makes it very easy in the design process for ITB children. KIFV 2026, go, go, go!
markdown_content: ## Overview: CLAW at CREA ITB Fashion Week 2026 This section introduces CLAW as a platform for ITB students to build skills in fashion, textile, and CREA during CREA ITB Fashion Week 2026. It highlights how CLAW 3D supports creative expression and learning across “soft goods” design. CLAW is presented as an initiative to empower students to develop knowledge in **fashion** and **textile**. Using **CLAW 3D**, students can express different types of **soft goods**, including **clothes**, **details**, **necklaces**, and **bags**. The platform is positioned as useful for anything that has **patterns** and is **sewn**, enabling visualization of designs directly in software. The talk also frames CLAW within ITB’s mission as a **fourth-generation university**, emphasizing development through **research**. It suggests that future university advancement depends on higher technology—specifically through **digital** approaches. ## CLAW 3D Capabilities for Soft Goods and Pattern Visualization This section explains what kinds of products CLAW 3D can represent and how it visualizes pattern-based sewn items. It focuses on pattern visualization and the scope of soft goods design. With **CLAW 3D**, users can visualize designs for soft goods that follow a **pattern** and are **sewn**. The software supports expressing multiple categories of garment and accessory concepts, such as: - **Clothes** - **Details** - **Necklaces** - **Bags** The key idea is that students can translate design intent into a visual, software-based representation—making it easier to work with pattern-driven construction concepts before physical production. ## Digital Design Workflow: Pattern Creation, Sewing Simulation, and Fabric Behavior This section describes the workflow benefits of CLAW 3D, including pattern creation and simulation of how fabric behaves during sewing. It emphasizes speed, immediate feedback, and realistic previews. CLAW 3D is described as helpful for: 1. **Creating patterns** 2. **Simulating how fabric is sewn** 3. **Simulating how fabric sticks to fabric** The workflow is presented as faster than traditional iteration. The simulation can be performed **right away**, allowing users to see: - the **pattern immediately** - how the **result turns out** - overall design behavior without waiting for physical prototyping The speaker emphasizes that the process is **easy** and saves time, supporting efficiency for fashion engineers and students working in the fashion/textile environment. ## From Abstract Ideas to 2D/3D Visualization and Iteration This section explains how CLAW 3D helps convert abstract design ideas into **2D patterns** and **3D patterns**, and how iteration is handled without repeating physical steps unnecessarily. It also notes practical constraints like materials. Initially, students may struggle to abstract ideas into workable designs. CLAW 3D addresses this by visualizing concepts through: - **2D patterns** - **3D patterns** This visualization helps users see what the design “looks like” as the **final result**. If changes are needed—for example, if the design should be adjusted—CLAW 3D can support modifications **without requiring immediate re-sewing**, and it can reduce dependency on physical constraints such as: - not having the required **materials** Overall, this makes the design process **simpler** by enabling faster revisions and clearer visualization of outcomes. ## Research and Efficiency in Fashion/Textile Education This section connects CLAW’s digital tooling to ITB’s research-driven university development and the goal of improving efficiency in fashion/textile work. It frames CLAW 3D as a practical digital technology for students. The talk positions CLAW as part of ITB’s broader push toward **research** and higher **digital technology**. It suggests that future needs include technologies “much higher,” and one way to pursue that is through **digital** methods. For students and fashion engineers seeking efficiency, CLAW 3D is presented as a way to: - develop and test designs faster - simulate sewing and fabric behavior - present work to a **wider network** or **media** By making design output shareable and easier to iterate, CLAW 3D supports both educational development and practical workflow efficiency in the fashion and textile domain.
